newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan sees 1997 exports up 8.8 pct, imports down.
newsitem.headline: Jordan sees 1997 exports up 8.8 pct, imports down.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti said on Monday the value of Jordanian exports would rise at least 8.8 percent in 1997 while its import bill looked set to fall.
Kabariti told the official Petra news agency Jordan expected to find new markets for its exports in 1997. He gave no details.

He said import bills would fall because world grain prices had dipped from their record highs in the first half of 1996. Bread is a staple food for Jordan's 4.2 million people and grain purchases form a large part of imports.

Jordan's Central Bank put exports in January to October 1996 at 845 million dinars ($1.19 billion) compared to 1.00 billion dinars for the whole of 1995. Imports in the first ten months of last year stood at 2.61 billion dinars, already above the 2.59 billion imports of 1995.
